column2: But how he now sees, we do not know, or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him; he is of age. He will speak for himself.”
His parents said these things because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed him as Christ, that person would be put out of the synagogue.
For this reason his parents said, “He is of age; ask him.”
So for a second time they called the man who had been blind and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
He answered, “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. One thing I know: though I was blind, now I see.”
Then they said to him, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
He answered them, “I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You do not also want to become his disciples, do you?”
Then they insulted him and said, “You are that man’s disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
We know that God has spoken to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he is from.”
The man answered them, “Now this is an amazing thing: you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes.
